balance_desc: Calls between federated nodes are free. Calls to regular phones (PSTN) require balance.
demo_disabled: Install and download buttons are disabled in the demo node.
demo_warning: Demo Node: Federated services are for visualization only in the demo. Services cannot be installed, uninstalled, or managed from the demo node.
help_add_note: Note: the one-click installer requires the service to have a public Docker image. If the service does not use Docker, it can only be installed manually with "Download" and following the instructions.
help_add_service_desc: The catalog is defined in the backend code (internal/api/services_catalog.go). To add a new service:
help_add_service_q: How do I add a service that is not in the catalog?
help_add_step2: Add an entry to the slice
help_add_step4: Restart the node. The new service appears automatically in the catalog.
help_catalog_desc: It is a list of more than 20 self-hosted services that you can install on your node's server. Each service replaces a commercial platform (YouTube, WhatsApp, Netflix, etc.) but without ads, without surveillance and without intermediary companies. The data stays on your server.
help_delta_chat: Delta Chat: WhatsApp-style chat via email
help_delta_chat_desc: Delta Chat is a client (app) that is installed on each member's phone or PC, not on the server. To use it:
help_delta_note: There is no need to configure servers manually in Delta Chat. Just email and password. The chat looks just like WhatsApp: messages, photos, files, groups, calls.
help_delta_step1: Install Mailu or Mailcow on the node.
help_delta_step2: The admin creates an email account for each member.
help_delta_step3: Each member installs Delta Chat on their phone (Google Play, App Store, F-Droid).
help_delta_step4: In Delta Chat, enter their email@{nodeDomain} and password.
help_delta_step5: Delta Chat automatically connects to the node's IMAP/SMTP server.
help_delta_step6: To chat with someone from another village: add their email@other-village.com.
help_download_docker_desc: If you prefer to install the service manually on another server, click Download. A file with the docker-compose.yml and a README.md with instructions is downloaded.
help_email_chat_desc: (Delta Chat): app that is installed on each member's phone/PC. It looks like WhatsApp but uses the node's email server.
help_email_clients_desc: After installing Mailu or Mailcow, members configure their email clients as follows:
help_email_clients_recommended: Recommended clients: Thunderbird (PC), K-9 Mail (Android), Mail (iOS). Most auto-configure via Autoconfig/Autodiscover: just enter the email and password, and the client finds the server automatically.
help_email_components_desc: Email has three components that are installed separately:
help_email_pass: Password: the one assigned by the admin
help_email_server_desc: (Mailu or Mailcow): installed on the node. Receives and sends emails. Creates accounts for each member.
help_email_webmail_desc: (SnappyMail): web interface to read email from the browser without installing anything.
help_federation_desc: Services that support ActivityPub (PeerTube, Mastodon, Pixelfed, Friendica, Lemmy, BookWyrm, Funkwhale) can federate with other villages. This means content published in one village is visible from other federated villages. To federate services, each village must install the same service and configure federation between them.
help_how_install: How do I install a service?
help_install_step1: Find the service in the catalog (use the search or filter by category).
help_install_step2: Click Details to see RAM, disk, port and subdomain requirements.
help_install_step3: Verify that your server has enough RAM and disk.
help_install_step4: Click Install. The system generates the docker-compose.yml and instructions.
help_install_step5: The service appears as Running or Stopped. You can start, stop or uninstall it whenever you want.
help_mail_choice: If your node has little RAM, install Mailu. If you have another server with more RAM, install Mailcow there. Both federate with any email server in the world.
help_mail_rules_desc: From the Mailu or Mailcow admin panel you can configure:
help_mail_rules_note: These rules are configured from the email server's web panel, not from the governance system.
help_mailu_vs_mailcow: Mailu vs Mailcow: which to choose?
help_permission_desc: To install, uninstall, start or stop services you need the permission
help_permission_desc2: The Assembly decides who has this permission through the system's roles and departments.
help_subdomain_desc: Each service has a suggested subdomain. If you have OpenWrt configured, the subdomain is registered automatically in the intranet.
my_services_active_subs_desc: Summary of your active services and upcoming charges.
my_services_cancel_confirm: Are you sure you want to cancel this service?
my_services_mandatory_desc: These services are provided by Assembly organizations. All members must pay them monthly.
my_services_voluntary_desc: You can subscribe or cancel anytime.
no_extensions: No extensions. Create one for each member.
no_pstn: No PSTN gateways configured. Calls between federated nodes are free.
no_services: No services found. Try another search.
pos_important_desc: This POS only processes TQ (not traditional money or cryptocurrencies). It is downloaded from this node and configured with its address, but accepts payments from members of any federated node.
pstn_desc: Allows calling landline/mobile numbers outside the federated network. Requires an account with a SIP trunk provider.
routes_desc: To call another village, dial its code + extension (e.g.: 105-2001)
search_placeholder: Search service or what it replaces...
subdomain_hint: If you have OpenWrt, this subdomain is registered automatically
subtitle: Replace commercial services with self-hosted and federated alternatives
title: Federated Services
uninstall_confirm_body: The Docker container will be stopped and removed. Service data may be lost.
